title: The Rising Tide Cave
story: In a shell-lined sea cave, four otter-folk pups are huddled on a ledge 9 feet above the water, while Skarrowgulp the Cave Gulper gulps down seawater and spouts it back out, raising the pool 4.5 feet every minute. Mr 6 pries open an old drain rune in the cave floor, which sucks 3 feet of water per minute back out to sea.
question: With water pouring in at 4.5 feet per minute and draining out at 3 feet per minute, how many minutes until the water reaches the pups' ledge 9 feet up?
solution: Water comes in at 4.5 feet per minute and leaves at 3, so it really rises 4.5 - 3 = 1.5 feet each minute.
The ledge is 9 feet up, so 9 / 1.5 = 6 minutes.
Mr 6 has 6 minutes to get the pups out.
praise: Dividing to find the time was the right instinct — the drain rune's 3 feet just needed to be subtracted first.
hint: The water is coming in AND going out at the same time. Find how much the pool truly gains in one single minute before you divide.
victory: Mr 6 knots his cape into a sling and swings all four pups out with a full minute to spare — six minutes, calculated by a six. Skarrowgulp, impressed, spits the rest of the water out the cave mouth and asks to be taught fractions.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight swinging four otter pups to safety on a caped sling inside a glittering sea cave as a huge whiskered gulper monster spouts a column of seawater, dramatic blue-green light on rising water.
